nodes.text: Mind the wet ink — that's someone's inheritance drying. Welcome to Inks & Charts: deeds, charters, wills, and honest maps. Three of those are promises and one's a confession. I'll let you decide which.
What can I draw up for you?

An honest map shows its ignorance. Mine have blank patches labeled *I have not been here and neither has anyone I trust* — you'd be amazed how rare that sentence is in cartography. A pretty map that guesses is worse than no map: it sends confident people into the Thornveil at dusk. The Guildhall buys my charts precisely because they admit what they don't know.

Every deed on Lantern Row, half the mining claims on the Emberway, and the boundary rolls the Guildhall's records room and I politely fight about. Seventeen disputed stones between us. I'm right about sixteen. The seventeenth I defend purely on principle, because the day I concede a stone without a survey is the day my ink stops meaning anything.

Keep your own chart. Mark it as you walk. A bought map shows where the cartographer was brave; yours shows where *you* were, and no one can sell it, steal it, or argue with it. When you've filled a whole province with your own footsteps, come back and tell me what my maps got wrong. I'll pay in ink and gratitude. Mostly ink.
Ink and luck. The blank patches are waiting for somebody — might as well be you.
